doc_description: Adobe Inc. (Nasdaq: ADBE) Annual Report on Form 10‑K for the fiscal year ended December 2, 2022, detailing its Digital Media (Creative & Document Cloud) and Digital Experience businesses, comprehensive risk factors and controls, KPMG‑audited financials ($17.6B revenue with strong subscription/ARR growth), market risk and FX hedging, major capital allocation (substantial share repurchases and fixed‑rate notes), properties and workforce, and the pending ~$20B acquisition of Figma.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- Filing overview: Adobe Inc.’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 2, 2022, filed with the SEC; Commission File No. 0-15175; common stock listed on NASDAQ under “ADBE.”
- Company and compliance status: Well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer; has filed required reports and submitted required interactive data files; auditor attestation of internal control over financial reporting; not a shell company.
- Capital and market data: Aggregate market value held by non-affiliates as of June 3, 2022 was $159.00 billion; 457.8 million shares outstanding as of January 6, 2023.
- Incorporation and headquarters: Incorporated in Delaware; principal executive offices at 345 Park Avenue, San Jose, CA 95110-2704; global operations across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC; investor materials and SEC filings available on adobe.com (not incorporated by reference).
- Documents incorporated by reference: Portions of the 2023 Proxy Statement included in Part III.
- Table of contents highlights: Part I (Business; Risk Factors; Properties; Legal Proceedings; Mine Safety); Part II (Market for Common Equity and Issuer Purchases; MD&A; Market Risk; Financial Statements; Controls and Procedures; Other Information; Foreign Jurisdictions Preventing Inspections); Part III (Directors and Governance; Compensation; Ownership; Related Transactions; Fees and Services); Part IV (Exhibits and Schedules; 10-K Summary; Signatures; Trademarks).
- Forward-looking statements: Cautions regarding statements on product plans, growth, market opportunities, FX impacts, strategic investments, positioning, customer metrics, ARR, revenue growth, and COVID-19 effects; identifies risk factors in Item 1A; no obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by law.
- Business overview: Founded in 1982, Adobe is a diversified software company serving creative professionals, communicators, businesses, governments, and consumers with tools to create, manage, deliver, measure, optimize, engage, and transact across devices and digital media formats.
- Go-to-market and revenue models: Direct enterprise sales and web sales (including app stores); SaaS and managed services (cloud-based), term subscriptions, and pay-per-use; distribution via distributors, VARs, SIs, ISVs, retailers, developers, and OEMs; technology licensing to hardware, software, and service providers; products available on desktop, mobile, and web.
- Strategic focus areas: Investment focused on two growth areas, beginning with Digital Media—providing products, services, and solutions for content creation, publishing, promotion, and collaboration (centered around Adobe Creative Cloud). The section continues beyond the excerpt.

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase: Founded in 1982, Adobe is one of the largest and most diversified software companies in the world.
structure.summary:
- Forward-looking statements caution, with references to SEC filings and no obligation to update.
- Business overview: Adobe as a global, diversified software company serving creatives, communicators, businesses, governments and consumers via SaaS, managed services, subscriptions, and select perpetual licenses; sold direct and through channels; global presence across Americas, EMEA and APAC.
- Strategic focus: two primary growth areas—Digital Media (Creative Cloud, Document Cloud) and Digital Experience (Experience Cloud), plus a legacy Publishing and Advertising segment.
- Digital Media opportunity and strategy: capitalize on creator economy, democratize creativity, enable collaboration, expand web/mobile workflows; product-led growth and data-driven marketing; grow Creative Cloud across pro and novice users (e.g., Adobe Express, Substance 3D, Frame.io integrations, web versions of Photoshop/Illustrator, AI-powered features); scale Document Cloud by enhancing Acrobat/Acrobat web, Liquid Mode, Scan, and Acrobat Sign; deepen partnerships (Microsoft, Workday, ServiceNow, Notarize).
- Digital Experience opportunity and strategy: support enterprise digital transformation and real-time personalization at scale; pillars include Data/Insights/Audiences (Analytics, CJA, Audience Manager, Real-time CDP), Content/Commerce (Experience Manager, Commerce), Customer Journeys (Marketo Engage, Campaign, Target, Journey Optimizer), and Marketing Workflows (Workfront); leverage Adobe Experience Platform and Adobe Sensei AI; go-to-market through direct sales and extensive partner ecosystem; focus on B2C, B2B and mid-market growth with tighter integrations (including Creative Cloud and Acrobat Sign).
- Publishing and Advertising: legacy offerings in eLearning, technical publishing, web conferencing, forms, high-end printing (PostScript/PDF), and Advertising Cloud DSP; OEM licensing and usage-based models.
- Competition: intense, rapidly evolving landscape across all segments; competition from large enterprises, point solutions, free/mobile/web-native tools and internal builds; key factors include features, integration, UX, security, scalability, pricing and ecosystem strength.
- Principal products and services: Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Lightroom, Illustrator, Fresco, InDesign, Premiere Pro, Premiere Rush, After Effects, Adobe Express, Stock, Substance 3D, Frame.io, Behance); Document Cloud (Acrobat, Acrobat web, Acrobat Reader, Scan, Acrobat Sign); Experience Cloud components (Experience Platform; Analytics, CJA, Audience Manager, Real-time CDP; Experience Manager Sites/Assets/Forms/Screens; Commerce; Marketo Engage; Campaign; Target; Journey Optimizer; Workfront).
- Operations and go-to-market: direct and channel sales, adobe.com as key motion, teams/enterprise offerings, global field offices; majority subscription revenue; no single customer >10% of revenue or receivables.
- Services and support: consulting/professional services, customer success management, technical support tiers, developer enablement, and extensive digital learning/training programs; strong partner enablement via Solution Partner Program.
- Investments and R&D: combine internal development with acquisitions and IP licensing; continuous innovation required due to fast tech change.
- IP protection and licensing: mix of patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets; click-through and signed agreements; SaaS model helps counter piracy.
- Human capital: ~29,239 employees (51% U.S., 49% international), 2022 attrition 11.7%; Adobe For All DEI initiatives with representation goals; pay parity achieved (global gender; U.S. URM); comprehensive compensation/benefits and wellbeing; hybrid work model; learning and career development (Learning Fund, internal mobility).
- Corporate information access: SEC filings available on Adobe’s investor site.
- Executive leadership: listings and bios of key officers including CEO/Chairman Shantanu Narayen and presidents/C-suite leaders.
- Risk factors snapshot: need to innovate amid intense competition, shifting platforms (mobile/web), evolving standards, pricing pressure and potential disruption from new technologies.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase: As previously discussed, our actual results could differ materially from our forward-looking statements.
structure.summary:
- Executive profile: Mark Garfield (52), Senior Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. Prior roles at Cloudflare (VP Finance), Symantec (SVP & CAO), Brightstar (SVP & CAO), AMD (Director of Finance), earlier roles at LoudCloud and EY; Adobe Foundation board member; B.A. in Business Economics, UC Santa Barbara.

- Item 1A. Risk Factors (summary of key themes):
  - Market and growth risks: intense competition and pricing pressure; need for rapid innovation and platform adaptation (mobile/web/device OS changes); technology shifts and potential obsolescence; limitations on tracking technologies (cookies/ad blockers) affecting marketing and fraud prevention; dependence on content marketplaces (e.g., Adobe Stock) and their network effects; reputational risks from misuse of tools (e.g., DeepFakes).
  - AI-related risks: ethical, social, regulatory and cost challenges of embedding AI and generative AI; potential need for proprietary datasets, attribution/remuneration frameworks for creators; higher compute costs; evolving regulation.
  - M&A and investment risks: execution, integration and realization of synergies; retention of people/customers/partners; due diligence gaps; security vulnerabilities in acquired products; regulatory approvals (including pending Figma acquisition); geopolitical/trade restrictions; acquisition-related costs and impairments.
  - Security and operational risks: data breaches at Adobe or third-party providers; reliance on Adobe/third-party data centers and content delivery; outages, data loss/corruption and service-level breaches; supply chain disruptions (pandemic, geopolitical); escalating and sophisticated cyber threats (including nation-state actors), vulnerabilities, phishing/social engineering; need for security certifications and ongoing investment.
  - Sales execution risks: extended, complex enterprise sales cycles (Experience Cloud, Platform, ETLAs); quarter-end sales concentration; unpredictability in timing and collections.
  - Third-party/partner ecosystem: dependence on strategic partners, distributors, OEMs and app stores (Apple App Store, Google Play) with changing terms and potential competition; quality and perception risks from outsourced customer support; channel management, compliance and financial health of partners.
  - Talent and workforce: attraction/retention of key leaders and skilled staff; competition for talent, global hiring dynamics; hybrid work model challenges to culture, security and productivity; international expansion and scaling.
  - International exposure: foreign currency volatility, inflation, sanctions, trade barriers, political instability and conflicts; export controls; data flow restrictions; infrastructure and corruption risks; language/localization costs; weaker IP protection in some jurisdictions.
  - Legal and regulatory compliance: complex global regimes (trade, sanctions, anti-corruption, antitrust, privacy, data residency, content, securities); evolving privacy/data protection laws (GDPR, PIPL, CCPA/CPRA, other US states); cross-border transfer constraints (SCCs, TADPF and similar); potential joint liability with customers/suppliers; contractual burdens and impact on product design and demand.
  - Intellectual property: piracy and unauthorized use; protection of patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets and source code; risk of disclosure undermining competitive position; third-party IP claims and PAE litigation leading to costs, injunctions, unfavorable licenses and indemnities.
  - Accounting and tax: changes in GAAP standards and interpretations impacting reporting, systems and results; global tax law changes (including OECD/EU actions) affecting effective tax rates and structures; ongoing tax audits and uncertainties.
  - Government contracting: complex procurement rules, audits and investigations; risk of penalties, termination, suspension or debarment.
  - Financial performance and structure: subscription renewal and upsell variability; ratable revenue recognition delaying impact of bookings; FX exposure and imperfect hedging; potential impairments of goodwill/intangibles; leverage and covenant compliance on issued notes and revolving credit facility; credit rating changes; market-driven impairment risk to investment portfolio.
  - General and macro risks: catastrophic events (pandemics, earthquakes, cyber incidents, extreme weather) disrupting operations, especially given concentration in Bay Area and Salt Lake regions; climate change effects (wildfires, power outages) and related stakeholder/ reporting expectations; economic uncertainty (inflation, interest rates, recessions, conflicts) impacting demand, collections and banking partners; stock price volatility and potential for securities litigation.

structure.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes thereto.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Item 7 MD&A for fiscal 2022, read with Consolidated Financial Statements; 2021 vs. 2020 discussion referenced to prior 10-K.
- Critical accounting policies and estimates:
  - Revenue recognition: Judgment in identifying performance obligations for offerings that bundle on-premise/on-device software with cloud services. For Creative Cloud and Document Cloud, licenses and cloud services are not distinct; revenue recognized ratably over the subscription term. Rationale cites integrated cloud features (e.g., Creative Cloud Libraries, shared reviews, cloud rendering, Sensei AI/ML).
  - Business combinations: Purchase price allocation to tangible/intangible assets and assumed liabilities based on fair value; key estimates include future cash flows, development costs, customer attrition/growth, trade names, asset use, discount rates. Deferred revenue fair value measured via cost build-up (fulfillment costs plus a normal margin).
  - Income taxes: Asset/liability method; significant judgment for current/deferred taxes and valuation allowances; reserves for uncertain tax positions and ongoing assessments of audits; effective tax rate sensitive to law changes and audit outcomes.
  - Recent accounting pronouncements referenced to Note 1.
- Acquisitions: Frame.io acquired for ~$1.24B (integrated into Digital Media); Workfront for ~$1.52B (integrated into Digital Experience).
- Results of operations—overview:
  - Strong demand across Digital Media and Digital Experience; continued growth in subscription revenue.
  - Digital Media:
    - Creative Cloud leadership; introduction of Adobe Express; strategy focuses on new user acquisition, deeper value, marketplace (Adobe Stock), and ARR growth.
    - Document Cloud: Acrobat, Acrobat Sign, Scan; subscription and perpetual options.
    - DDOM used to drive awareness, acquisition, engagement, and retention.
    - ARR is key metric; definition provided and measured at fixed FX rates per year.
    - ARR impact from Russia-Ukraine actions: $87M reduction (Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine).
    - Ending ARR (FY22): Creative $11.60B; Document Cloud $2.37B; Total Digital Media $13.97B (would be $13.26B at FY23 FX).
    - FY22 revenue: Creative $10.46B (+10% YoY), Document Cloud $2.38B (+21% YoY), Total Digital Media $12.84B (+11% YoY).
  - Digital Experience:
    - Experience Cloud spans data/insights, content/commerce, customer journeys, and marketing workflow (including Workfront).
    - Go-to-market via direct sales and partner ecosystem.
    - FY22 revenue $4.42B (+14% YoY); subscription revenue $3.88B (+15% YoY).
  - Macroeconomic conditions: FX headwinds due to global events (Russia-Ukraine war, COVID-19, inflation/central bank actions) negatively impacted FY22 and expected to continue into FY23; uncertainty remains.
- FY22 financial performance highlights:
  - Digital Media ARR +$1.82B (15%) to $13.97B.
  - Digital Experience revenue +$555M (14%).
  - RPO $15.19B (+9%).
  - Cost of revenue $2.17B (+16%) driven by hosting/data centers and compensation.
  - Operating expenses $9.34B (+15%) on compensation and marketing.
  - Operating cash flow $7.84B (+8%).
- Revenue details:
  - Total revenue $17.61B (+12%); subscription $16.39B (93% of total, +12%); product $532M (3%, -4%); services/other $686M (4%, +4%).
  - Subscription by segment: Digital Media $12.39B (+12%), Digital Experience $3.88B (+15%), Publishing & Advertising $123M (-16%).
  - Segments: Digital Media $12.84B (73% of total, +11%); Digital Experience $4.42B (25%, +14%); Publishing & Advertising $342M (2%, -14%).
  - Digital Media mix: Creative Cloud $10.46B (+10%), Document Cloud $2.38B (+21%).
  - Geography: Americas $10.25B (+14%), EMEA $4.59B (+8%), APAC $2.76B (+9%).
  - FX reduced revenue by ~$486M; cash flow hedging gains offset ~$176M.
- Costs and expenses:
  - Cost of subscription up 20% (hosting/data centers +9 pts; amortization +4; base comp +3; incentive comp +1; royalties +2).
  - Cost of services/other up 8% (compensation and professional fees).
  - R&D $2.99B (+18%) on compensation, incentives, and professional fees.
  - Sales & marketing $4.97B (+15%) on marketing spend and compensation.
  - G&A $1.22B (+12%) on professional/consulting (including Figma transaction costs), incentives, base comp; partially offset by event cancellations.
- Non-operating items and taxes:
  - Interest expense ~$112M; investment gains/losses, net $(19)M; other income $41M (higher interest income).
  - Income tax provision $1.25B; effective tax rate 21% (up ~6 pts due to lower stock-based comp tax benefits). Continued impact of U.S. research credit and state taxes. Notes 2020 IP transfer to Ireland creating $1.35B deferred tax assets; valuation allowance $402M at FY22; unrecognized tax benefits $321M gross; possible $25M reduction over next 12 months; ongoing exposure to global tax law changes.
- Liquidity and capital resources:
  - Cash/cash equivalents $4.24B; short-term investments $1.86B; working capital $868M; equity $14.05B (as of Dec 2, 2022).
  - Cash flows FY22: operating $7.84B; investing $(0.57)B; financing $(6.83)B; net increase in cash $0.39B.
  - Uses/sources: primary source revenue receipts; uses include stock repurchases, payroll, hosting; additional uses: acquisitions, capex, taxes on equity settlements; source: ESPP proceeds.
  - Liquidity outlook: cash, operations, and credit facility expected sufficient for next 12 months; portfolio comprised of diversified high-grade securities managed by external managers; ongoing investment in growth and selective M&A.
  - Pending acquisition: Figma for ~$20B (half cash/half stock) plus ~6M RSUs; reverse termination fee $1B under certain conditions; expected close in 2023 subject to regulatory approvals; cash portion to be financed with cash and short-term debt; plan to repurchase at least to offset employee equity dilution while pending.
  - Revolving Credit Agreement: $1.5B unsecured facility through June 30, 2027 (expandable to $2.0B); no borrowings outstanding at FY22.
  - Debt: $4.15B senior notes outstanding (carrying value ~$4.13B); interest payable semiannually; $500M due Feb 1, 2023 classified as current; intent to repay at or before due date.
  - Contractual obligations: non-cancellable purchase obligations $6.09B (primarily hosting/data centers); operating leases $548M; U.S. Tax Act transition tax ~$313M payable through FY26; R&D capitalization starting FY23 expected to increase cash taxes partially offset by FDII benefit; Inflation Reduction Act book minimum tax (effective FY24) and buyback excise tax being evaluated.
- Stock repurchase program:
  - $15B authorization through FY24 (approved Dec 2020).
  - FY22 repurchases: 15.7M shares (mix of structured and accelerated programs); year-end structured prepayment balance $583M; post year-end ASR of $1.4B with initial 3.2M shares delivered; ~$5.15B remaining authorization after ASR completion.
- Indemnifications: Standard IP infringement indemnities to customers/partners and officer/director indemnification; historically not significant; D&O insurance in place.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase: All market risk sensitive instruments were entered into for non-trading purposes.
structure.summary:
- Focus: Item 7A—Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk, covering foreign currency and interest rate risk for non-trading activities.
- Foreign currency risk:
  - Revenue exposure by currency (in millions): Euro (€2,487 in 2022; €2,209 in 2021; €1,887 in 2020), Japanese Yen (¥118,456; ¥104,829; ¥88,640), British Pounds (£737; £669; £562), Australian Dollars ($876; $768; $645).
  - Hedging program uses options and forwards to hedge forecasted foreign currency revenues/expenses and to hedge recognized monetary assets/liabilities; not used for speculation and does not fully offset FX movements.
  - As of Dec 2, 2022, total notional outstanding FX contracts: $3.25B, including $1.32B (EUR), $602M (INR), $480M (GBP), $394M (JPY), $338M (AUD), $112M (other); maturities through Nov 2023.
  - Counterparty credit risk mitigated via master netting and collateral agreements.
  - Sensitivity (10% USD move) on FX derivatives as of Dec 2, 2022: +10% USD → +$75M in hedging instruments’ fair value; −10% USD → +$17M.
  - Natural hedges: generally do not hedge local expenses where revenues offset; long-term net investment exposures of $770M (2022) and $749M (2021) remain unhedged.
- Cash flow hedges:
  - Use purchased options/forwards to hedge forecasted revenue (EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD) and expenses (INR) with maturities up to 12 months.
  - Hedge accounting: changes in fair value recorded in AOCI and reclassified to revenue/operating expenses when the forecasted transactions occur.
  - No net gains/losses recognized in 2022 for hedges of forecasted transactions that did not occur.
- Non-designated hedges:
  - FX forwards used to hedge non-functional currency monetary assets/liabilities; fair value changes recognized in other income (expense); maturities 180 days or less.
- Interest rate risk:
  - Short-term investments: $1.86B in debt securities as of Dec 2, 2022.
  - Sensitivity to an immediate parallel yield curve shift of 150 bps: +150 bps → ~$20M decrease in market value; −150 bps → ~$20M increase.
- Debt:
  - Senior notes outstanding: $4.15B fixed-rate as of Dec 2, 2022; minimal earnings risk from rate changes.
  - Carrying value $4.13B; estimated fair value $3.88B.

structure.title: Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.heading: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.start_phrase:
All financial statement schedules have been omitted, since the required information is not applicable or is not present in

structure.summary:
- Scope and structure: Adobe Inc.’s Item 8 includes the full set of audited consolidated financial statements for fiscal years 2022, 2021, and 2020; accompanying notes; and KPMG LLP’s unqualified audit opinions on the financial statements and internal control over financial reporting, with one critical audit matter related to performance obligations in cloud-enabled subscriptions.
- Consolidated financial highlights (FY2022 vs. FY2021):
  - Assets/Liabilities/Equity: Total assets $27.2B; total liabilities $13.1B; stockholders’ equity $14.1B.
  - Revenue and earnings: Revenue $17.6B (Subscription $16.4B), gross profit $15.4B, operating income $6.1B, net income $4.8B; diluted EPS $10.10.
  - Cash: Cash and cash equivalents $4.24B; short-term investments $1.86B.
  - Deferred revenue: Current $5.30B; long-term $0.12B; total ~$5.41B.
  - Debt: $4.15B senior notes outstanding; $500M due Feb 2023 (current); new $1.5B undrawn revolving credit facility.
  - Cash flows: Operating $7.84B; investing $(0.57)B; financing $(6.83)B; ending cash $4.24B.
- Segment and geographic results:
  - Revenue by segment (2022): Digital Media $12.84B (Creative Cloud $10.46B; Document Cloud $2.38B), Digital Experience $4.42B, Publishing & Advertising $0.34B.
  - Gross margin by segment: Digital Media 96%, Digital Experience 66%, Publishing & Advertising 70%.
  - Revenue by geography (2022): Americas $10.25B, EMEA $4.59B, APAC $2.76B.
- Key accounting policies and estimates:
  - Revenue recognition across SaaS, cloud-hosted, on-premise licenses, maintenance, consulting, training, and advertising; significant judgment on distinct performance obligations (Creative Cloud/Document Cloud treated as single integrated obligations recognized ratably).
  - Standalone selling price, variable consideration, principal vs. agent assessments, contract acquisition costs (capitalized commissions, 5-year amortization), and use of practical expedients.
  - Leases (operating only), goodwill and intangibles impairment testing (no impairments), property and equipment depreciation, treasury stock accounting, foreign currency, derivatives, and credit risk concentrations.
- Contracting metrics:
  - Trade receivables net $2.07B (including $93M unbilled).
  - Contract assets $97M; refund liabilities $106M.
  - Remaining performance obligations ~$15.19B; ~72% expected to be recognized within 12 months (excluding certain enterprise arrangements).
  - Capitalized contract acquisition costs $629M (amortization $238M in 2022).
- Acquisitions:
  - Pending: Agreement to acquire Figma for ~$20B (half cash/half stock) plus ~6M RSUs; subject to regulatory approval; $1B reverse termination fee under certain conditions; intended to join Digital Media.
  - Completed: Frame.io (2021) for ~$1.24B (allocated primarily to goodwill and purchased technology); Workfront (2020) for ~$1.52B (noted allocation to customer relationships and goodwill).
- Investments and fair value:
  - Highly liquid, investment-grade portfolio; cash equivalents largely money market funds.
  - Detailed fair value hierarchy disclosures; most debt securities Level 2; derivatives measured at fair value.
- Derivatives and hedging:
  - Cash flow hedges of foreign currency exposures (EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, INR) and prior Treasury lock; non-designated forwards hedge balance sheet exposures.
  - Net gains/losses recognized in OCI and reclassified to revenue/expenses consistent with hedge accounting.
- Property, equipment, leases:
  - Property and equipment, net $1.91B; depreciation expense $189M (2022); significant capital projects in progress.
  - Operating lease liabilities PV $504M; weighted average remaining term 7 years; lease expense $121M (2022).
- Goodwill and intangibles:
  - Goodwill $12.79B (no impairment; primarily Digital Media and Digital Experience).
  - Other intangibles, net $1.45B; amortization expense $405M in 2022; future amortization schedule provided.
- Accrued expenses:
  - Major components include bonuses, compensation/benefits, corporate marketing, taxes, and refund liabilities.
- Income taxes:
  - Tax provision $1.25B (2022); income before taxes $6.01B (domestic $1.96B; foreign $4.05B).
  - Deferred tax assets, net $0.75B; valuation allowance $402M (primarily state credits).
  - Noted 2020 intra-entity IP transfers to Ireland creating significant deferred tax assets; reconciliation of effective tax rate drivers; unrecognized tax benefits $321M.
- Benefit plans:
  - 401(k) matching ($76M in 2022) and non-qualified deferred compensation plan; plan assets and liabilities disclosed.
- Stock-based compensation and equity programs:
  - RSUs and performance share programs under 2019 Equity Incentive Plan; ESPP with 15% discount/look-back.
  - Stock-based compensation expense $1.44B (allocated across functions); unrecognized cost $2.83B over ~2.3 years.
  - RSU and performance share activity and valuation methodologies (Monte Carlo for TSR awards).
- Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss):
  - Components include AFS securities, cash flow hedge adjustments, and foreign currency translation; 2022 net AOCI loss increased primarily from FX translation.
- Share repurchases:
  - Board authorization up to $15B through FY2024.
  - 2022 repurchases: 15.7M shares, $6.55B (including $2.4B ASR); subsequent ASR of $1.4B executed post-year-end; $5.15B remaining authority thereafter.
- Earnings per share:
  - Basic EPS $10.13; diluted EPS $10.10; share counts and anti-dilutive shares disclosed.
- Commitments and contingencies:
  - Non-cancellable purchase obligations ~$6.09B (notably hosting/data center services).
  - Royalty expense $228M (2022); standard indemnifications; summary of legal proceedings and risk.
- Debt and liquidity:
  - Senior notes: maturities in 2025, 2027, 2030; fair value ~$3.88B; no financial covenants; change-of-control provisions.
  - New $1.5B five-year unsecured revolving credit facility (undrawn at year-end), replacing prior facility.
- Non-operating items:
  - Interest expense $(112)M; investment gains/losses $(19)M; other income $41M (incl. interest income and FX).
- Auditor’s report (KPMG LLP, PCAOB ID 185):
  - Unqualified opinions on financial statements and internal control over financial reporting.
  - Critical audit matter: assessing whether cloud-enabled Creative Cloud/Document Cloud offerings constitute single integrated performance obligations; procedures included contract reviews, product demonstrations, and evaluation of integrated functionalities.
